profile.headline: Recent Stanford graduate with degrees in Biomechanical Engineering and Computer Science (A.I. track)

positions.title: Head of Product
positions.description: Our company, PIVA, partnered with Consumer Packaged Goods manufacturers and distributors based in Latin America with the goal of increasing the efficiency of their supply chain process through our technology solutions. We were an early stage company with a small team so my responsibilities were wide-ranging, but my primary focus was on building and shaping the products we offer our partners. Sold PIVA to a competitor after ~6 months on the ground.

positions.title: Teaching Assistant
positions.description: TA to Professor Hector Garcia-Molina for a Freshman Seminar oriented around the intersection of computer science and photography.

positions.title: Golf Instructor
positions.description: Golf Instructor for programs such as the Twin Lakes Junior Golf Program and Twin Lakes Golf School, where students ranged in age from second grade to seniors in high school to men and women in retirement. Also worked as a private swing coach for several students who started in larger programs but sought out one-on-one comprehensive swing analysis training.

positions.title: My Year Abroad
positions.description: During my senior year of high school in small town Wilmot, Wisconsin, my dream school, Stanford, turned down my first application. In response, I decided to take a year off of school. I wanted to learn in a setting outside a classroom through work, internships, and travel. Through generous help from two old family friends in Brisbane, Australia, I spent the majority of the next year working odd jobs, reapplying to schools back in the states, traveling, and doing brief internships for two engineering companies in the Brisbane area. I worked as a bartender, a waiter in a fine dining restaurant, a construction worker, a landscaper, a pool boy; I saved up enough to explore the Australian coast, the Outback, the streets and hills of Hong Kong, and did a solo trek to Everest Base Camp in Nepal. Spending a year out in the world (mostly) on my own was a great learning experience. And at the end of it all, Stanford answered my final question of what to do next by accepting my second application.

projects.title: Turner Fantasy Basketball
projects.description:
Turner Fantasy Basketball is a fantasy sports league that combines traditional fantasy basketball with a stock-market-like system for building and developing your roster. This is a salary cap system where each player has an associated value that rises and falls according to their on-court performance throughout the season. Competitors seek not only to have a roster that produces fantasy points but that also produces return-on-investment to gain an edge on the field.

I built and maintained this fantasy system primarily via spreadsheets, but also developed an accompanying website that is no longer active.

projects.title: Homemade Electric Longboard
projects.description: During my freshman year, Stanford inspired me to take up longboarding. I learned to enjoy it so much that I decided to, instead of buying an incredibly expensive commercial version, build myself an electrically powered longboard while I was home for the summer. I wanted to do it without any online kits or DIY guides, so I started from scratch (with the exception of the electric motor and the arduino) and tried to design and build my own. Through the process I became much more familiar with Arduino, C++, making structural modifications, and designing efficient circuits.

organizations.description: Held positions of Standards of Excellence Chair from November 2016 to April 2017, Vice President from November 2017 to April 2018, and then President from April to November 2018.
